thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Dow Falls 300 Points As Caterpillar Earnings Come Up Short; Fed In Focus

author: www.4-traders.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Dow Falls 300 Points As Caterpillar Earnings Come Up Short; Fed In Focus
text:
By Chris Matthews and Barbara Kollmeyer, MarketWatch
All 30 Dow components in the red; Oil prices slump as perceived riskier assets pull back
U.S. stocks retreated Monday morning as investors turned cautious in a busy week of earnings, economic reports -- including a midweek Federal Reserve policy update -- and a new round of U.S-China trade talks.
How are benchmark indexes trading?
The Dow Jones Industrial Average slid 317 points, or 1.3%, to 24,420, while the S&P 500 index fell 29 points, or 1.1%, to 2,636. The Nasdaq Composite dropped 108 points, or 1.5%, to 7,59
What's driving the market?
Friday's equity gains came after a surprise deal between U.S. President Donald Trump and congressional leaders to reopen the government until Feb. 15, for now ending a 35-day partial shutdown. Lawmakers will debate funding for an extension of the southern border wall.
But fears of another shutdown weren't far as Trump said he placed a 50-50 chance of a deal over border-wall funding being reached by a newly created board of 17 before the next government-funding deadline, in an interview with The Wall Street Journal (https://www.wsj.com/articles/lawmakers-to-debate-border-immigration-as-next-shutdown-threat-looms-11548614760?mod=hp_lead_pos1).
Meanwhile, some wariness ahead of a Fed meeting and a huge week for earnings were keeping investors cautious. The central bank will convene its two-day meeting on Tuesday, with no change in key interests expected. Attention is instead likely to focus on a news conference afterward with Fed Chairman Jerome Powell for any clues on future policy.
Earnings will swing into focus in a big way this week, starting with Caterpillar , whose shares are down 4.3% Monday, following an earnings report which showed the company missing fourth-quarter earnings forecasts.
After the close, Whirlpool is set to report. Investors will also hear this week from big names such as Facebook , Amazon and Apple Optimism over earnings also supported stocks last week.
Caterpillar earnings:Analysts expect good news on mining and an update on China
Trade will also come into focus, with talks aimed at resolving the impasse over Chinese technology ambitions and other issues expected to restart in Washington later in the week, headed up by U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer and Chinese Vice Premier Liu He.
Which other stocks are in focus?
Shares of Nvidia are down more than 14%, after the chipmaker said it expects to report $2.2 billion in fiscal fourth-quarter revenue, below its previous outlook of $2.7 billion.
Shares of Guess? Inc. are down 3.4% Monday, after the firm announced the departure of its CEO Victor Herrero, to be replaced by Carlo Alberini, currently the Chairman and CEO of Lucky Brand.
What data area ahead?
The Federal Reserve of Chicago's national activity index rose to 0.27 in December, up from 0.21 in November.
A Dallas Fed manufacturing survey is due at 10 a.m.
What are the analysts and traders saying?
U.S. stocks are "starting this week under some pressure, as Trump throws cold water on the chances of a shutdown deal, and after Chinese industrial production comes in light," wrote Dave Lutz, head of ETFs at JonesTrading, in a Monday-morning research note. "We have many unknowns ahead this week, with US China Trade Talks, The FOMC decision, US Jobs Report, 124 S&P names [reporting], a heavy tech reporting week with AAPL, AMZN and MSFT highlighting, and angst over tomorrow's Brexit vote."

How did the benchmarks perform last trading day?
On Friday , the Dow climbed 183.96 points, or 0.8%, to end at 24,737.20. The blue-chip index edged up 0.1% for the week, extending gains for a fifth week in a row. The S&P 500 rose 22.43 points, or 0.9%, to 2,664.76, down 0.2% on the week. The Nasdaq Composite climbed 91.40 points, or 1.3%, to 7,164.86, for a weekly rise of 0.1%.
How are other markets trading?
Meanwhile, stocks in Asia finished mixed, with the Nikkei 225 index closing down 0.6% and Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index ending flat. European stocks were lower , with the Stoxx Europe slipping 0.9%.
Crude-oil prices were under pressure , while gold futures inched higher, and the ICE U.S. Dollar Index , a measure of the U.S. currency against a basket of six major rivals, was flat. The British pound fell 0.2% to $1.3168 as ahead of a series of Brexit-related votes in the U.K. parliament that could delay or even cancel the country's exit from the European Union.
